Proposition
[properties of the bracket]

↗ lem:dc-ch0-5-3-antisymm ↗ lem:dc-ch0-5-3-jacobi-cyclic ↗ lem:dc-ch0-5-3-bilinear ↗ lem:dc-ch0-5-3-leibniz

1. ch0:5.3If $X,Y,Z$ are differentiable vector fields on $M$, $a,b\in \mathbb {R}$, and $f,g$ differentiable functions, then: (a) $[X,Y]=-[Y,X]$ (anticommutativity); (b) $[aX+bY,Z]=a[X,Z]+b[Y,Z]$ (linearity); (c) $[[X,Y],Z]+[[Y,Z],X]+[[Z,X],Y]=0$ (Jacobi identity); (d) $[fX,gY]=fg[X,Y]+fX(g)Y-gY(f)X$.
Proof

\sketch (a),(b) are immediate. For (c), expand $[[X,Y],Z]=XYZ-YXZ-ZXY+ZYX$ and $[X,[Y,Z]]+[Y,[Z,X]]=XYZ-XZY-YZX+ZYX+YZX-YXZ-ZXY+XZY$; the second members agree, and (c) follows using (a). For (d), $[fX,gY]=fX(gY)-gY(fX)=fgXY+fX(g)Y-gfYX-gY(f)X=fg[X,Y]+fX(g)Y-gY(f)X$.

□

For a differentiable vector field $X$ and $p\in M$, there exist a neighborhood $U$ of $p$, an interval $(-\delta ,\delta )$, and a differentiable map $\varphi :(-\delta ,\delta )\times U\to M$ such that $t\mapsto \varphi (t,q)$ is the unique curve with $\frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}=X(\varphi (t,q))$ and $\varphi (0,q)=q$. A curve $\alpha $ with $\alpha '(t)=X(\alpha (t))$, $\alpha (0)=q$, is a trajectory of $X$, and $\varphi _t(q)=\varphi (t,q)$ is the local flow of $X$.
